confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on web searches of aggregated cost-of-living sites (livingcost.org, citycost.org, nomad.watch). Those sites put local draft beer at about USD 2.55-2.78 (0.5 L), cappuccino at about USD 2.89-3.09, an inexpensive meal at about USD 7-8 and a mid-range dinner for two at about USD 32.60-35. Their figures are crowdsourced and the sites disagree slightly, so the anchors use central values. Beer was adjusted slightly upward because one site's pint estimate was higher and izakaya draft beer is commonly about JPY 500-600. A search of local izakaya listings found only promotional happy-hour beer and highball prices, which were not used as typical prices. No direct cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices were found. Those two anchors are estimated from the local price relationship to beer and general knowledge of Japanese regional izakaya and bar pricing (about JPY 600-900 for a cocktail and JPY 500-700 for house wine), so they are less certain. The JPY/USD rate implied by the cost-of-living sites was about 160 yen to the dollar. The rate in July 2026 may differ, which adds uncertainty to the USD values. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge only. No booking sites or listings were searched or inspected. They assume July summer-season demand in a mid-sized regional city with an onsen tourism draw (Dogo Onsen) and are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Matsuyama is a mid-sized regional Japanese city of about 500,000 people and is cheaper than Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto. Its pricing is comparable to similar regional capitals such as Okayama, Takamatsu and Kochi. Accommodation follows the typical Japanese regional pattern of budget guesthouses and business hotels, with some upward pressure in the Dogo Onsen area during summer.
